exposure: mode of birth (cesarean section vs. natural birth)
cohort: The study included 304 breastfeeding women in the immediate postpartum period during their stay in the maternity ward in Tarnowskie Gory, Poland.
finding: The study found that while most women reported good psychological well-being, a notable percentage experienced anxiety (11.9%), depressive (7.3%), and postpartum depression (5.9%) symptoms, which were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.
mod_finding: Women who gave birth by cesarean section were more likely to report problems negatively impacting their quality of life and health compared to those who had natural births.
cross-section timing: immediate postpartum period, during their stay in the maternity ward
